docs.title: anySeg
docs.text:
anySeg segments text into tokens, words and sentences with their positions in the source text: a Rust core and a Python package without dependencies. The text is never changed - every token and sentence is a span of the original string - and the tokens follow the conventions of Universal Dependencies, so the results can be compared with the treebanks and with the tools trained on them. One package serves all languages: the rules are shared, and a language brings its lists. Russian and Spanish are here, English follows.

Early version

Before 1.0 the API may change between 0.x versions.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Segmenter

    Tokens and sentences with their positions, documents of texts in batches on several threads, lists of your own abbreviations and tokens

    Segmenter

  • Document

    Tokens, words with the columns of CoNLL-U, sentences, paragraphs and lines; reading and writing CoNLL-U

    Document

  • Command

    anyseg for the terminal and pipelines: tokens, sentences or CoNLL-U of files and the standard input

    Command

  • Russian

    How Russian text is split: abbreviations, hyphenated words, numbers, the web, dialogue, lists and verse

    Russian

  • Spanish

    How Spanish text is split: multiword tokens, abbreviations, numbers, inverted marks, dialogue and articles

    Spanish

  • spaCy

    The tokenizer and the sentence starts of a spaCy pipeline, the conversion of documents

    spaCy

  • Comparison

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Python 3.11 or newer is required.

pip install anyseg

Prebuilt wheels need no Rust; building from source and the Rust crate: see Installation.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
CodeResult 
from anyseg import Segmenter

segmenter = Segmenter("ru")
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize("Кот спал в 1914 г. Затем ушёл, т. е. исчез.")]
segmenter.tokenize("Ёж идёт домой")

['Кот спал в 1914 г.', 'Затем ушёл, т. е. исчез.']
[Span(start=0, end=2, text='Ёж'), Span(start=3, end=7, text='идёт'), Span(start=8, end=13, text='домой')]

Positions are offsets in the characters of a Python string: text[span.start:span.end] == span.text. A document holds the tokens, the words with the columns of CoNLL-U, the sentences, the paragraphs and their lines:

CodeResult 
doc = segmenter.segment("Ёж идёт домой\n\nКот спит")
doc.set_columns(upos=["NOUN", "VERB", "ADV", "NOUN", "VERB"])
[sentence.text for sentence in doc.sentences], doc.words[1]

(['Ёж идёт домой', 'Кот спит'], Word(id=2, form='идёт', upos='VERB'))
Project structure
  • crates/anyseg - the core in Rust: tokens, sentences, the document model and CoNLL-U, with the lists of every language in data/ behind a Cargo feature
  • crates/anyseg-py - the Python module anyseg._anyseg built with PyO3
  • python/anyseg - the Python package
  • scripts - checking the installed package before publishing, and the licenses of the compiled crates
  • docs - MkDocs documentation
  • tests - tests of the Python package

docs.title: The anyseg command
docs.text:
anyseg --lang LANG [options] [file ...]

The command segments text from files or the standard input and writes its tokens, its sentences or CoNLL-U, for pipelines of Universal Dependencies tools. It comes with the package (pip install anyseg) and also runs as python -m anyseg; without Python, cargo install anyseg --features cli installs it.

echo "Кот спит в 1914 г. Затем ушёл" | anyseg -l ru -f sentences

Кот спит в 1914 г.
Затем ушёл

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Default Description -l, --lang - ISO 639-1 code of the language of the text: ru, es -f, --format tokens Output format: tokens, sentences, conllu -o, --output the standard output The result file; - is the standard output --abbreviations A file of more abbreviations, one per line; the option can be repeated --tokens A file of strings that are one token each, one per line; the option can be repeated -h, --help Show the help -V, --version Show the version

Files are read one after another; without files and in place of - the standard input is read. The input is in UTF-8: a file in another encoding (cp1251, UTF-16) is not segmented, and a single line with wrong bytes is segmented with U+FFFD in their place. In the files of lists, spaces around an entry are ignored, and blank lines and lines starting with # are skipped. An option value is written separately or attached: -f conllu, -fconllu, --format=conllu.

The text is segmented paragraph by paragraph: a paragraph is written as soon as a blank line or the end of the input closes it, so the command can be kept open and fed text. The result is the same as for the whole text, except for a text without blank lines longer than 256 KiB, such as a file with a sentence per line or a single long line. It is segmented in pieces, so that the memory stays bounded:

  • what depends on all the lines of a paragraph - verse and text wrapped at the width of the page - is decided by a piece;
  • the sentences and the paragraph go on across the pieces, except that a sentence longer than 256 KiB is cut, at a space or, if it has none, at a character, and the next piece reads as a new sentence, for the words of its first token too;
  • a number with a period and a bracket next to a cut may read differently, as a piece does not know what the text before it opened.

Lines end with LF, CR or CRLF.

In Windows PowerShell 5.1 the > redirection and a pipeline (Get-Content text.txt | anyseg -l ru) corrupt Cyrillic: pass the file as an argument and write the result with the -o option (in PowerShell 7 they work too). Text passed with echo in cmd comes in the console encoding: run chcp 65001 first.

docs.title: tokens
docs.text:
A token per line and a blank line after every sentence. A multiword token is one line: the words are in conllu.

идёт
домой

Кот
спит

docs.title: sentences
docs.text: A sentence per line, its line breaks turned into spaces, and a blank line between paragraphs.

docs.title: conllu
docs.text:
CoNLL-U as to_conllu writes it: every file starts with # newdoc, every paragraph with # newpar, and the sentences are numbered through the whole output; the space after a token goes to MISC, and a multiword token has its line before the lines of its words.

echo "Ёж идёт.  Кот" | anyseg -l ru -f conllu

# newdoc
# newpar
# sent_id = 1
# text = Ёж идёт.
1   Ёж  _   _   _   _   _   _   _   _
2   идёт    _   _   _   _   _   _   _   SpaceAfter=No
3   .   _   _   _   _   _   _   _   SpacesAfter=\s\s

# sent_id = 2
# text = Кот
1   Кот _   _   _   _   _   _   _   _

echo "Vengo del mar" | anyseg -l es -f conllu

# newdoc
# newpar
# sent_id = 1
# text = Vengo del mar
1   Vengo   _   _   _   _   _   _   _   _
2-3 del _   _   _   _   _   _   _   _
2   de  _   _   _   _   _   _   _   _
3   el  _   _   _   _   _   _   _   _
4   mar _   _   _   _   _   _   _   _

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code When 0 Success, or the reader of the output closed it (anyseg ... \| head) 1 A file does not open, is not in UTF-8 or has a line with wrong bytes, a list has a wrong entry, or the output cannot be written 2 Wrong options: no language, an unknown option or value

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text: anySeg against the segmenters of Russian and Spanish, rule-based and neural, on the test files of the treebanks of Universal Dependencies 2.18: SynTagRus, Taiga, GSD and PUD for Russian, AnCora, GSD and PUD for Spanish.

docs.title: How it is measured
docs.text:
• The raw text of a treebank is built from the text of its sentences: documents and paragraphs are separated by blank lines, the sentences of a paragraph are joined by spaces, and a paragraph stays on one line (the conllu_to_text.pl script of UD also wraps lines at 80 characters).
  • Tokens and sentences are scored with the evaluation script of the CoNLL 2018 shared task (F1). Sentence boundaries are scored as the positions of the sentence ends in the text (F1).
  • The scores follow the conventions of the treebanks, which anySeg follows too: a tool with other conventions loses points for them.
  • The rules of anySeg were chosen on the train and dev files; the test files are used only for this comparison.
  • Speed is measured on one thread of an Apple M3 Pro, on the raw text of SynTagRus test (903,085 characters, 157,706 tokens of the treebank) and of AnCora test (278,779 characters, 52,454 tokens). Tokens per second count the tokens of the treebank, the same for every tool.

Neural tools are marked with *. For Russian, Stanza, UDPipe and trankit use models trained on SynTagRus. For Spanish, Stanza uses its model combined and UDPipe a model trained on AnCora of UD 2.5, where «del» and «al» were not yet split. trankit is not in the Spanish tables, as its model could not be downloaded.

docs.title: Document
docs.text:
A segmented text: its tokens, its words with the columns of CoNLL-U, its sentences, its paragraphs and their lines. A document comes from Segmenter.segment, from Document.from_tokens or from read_conllu.

  • The text is never changed: tokens, sentences, paragraphs and lines are its spans, with positions in the characters of the Python string.
  • A token holds one word or, for a multiword token, several (Spanish «del» is «de» + «el»). The segmenter gives them where the language joins words in one token.
  • Sentences hold whole tokens, paragraphs - the parts of the text between blank lines - hold whole sentences, and lines are those of the paragraphs.
  • Words have the columns of CoNLL-U, empty until set; set_columns is the only change of a document, so a document can be shared between threads. It can be pickled with its columns, to go to another process; its parts cannot.
CodeResult 
from anyseg import Segmenter

doc = Segmenter("ru").segment("Ёж идёт домой.\nКот спит\n\nУтро  наступило")
doc, [sentence.text for sentence in doc.sentences]
[(line.text, line.break_before) for line in doc.lines]

(Document(tokens=8, words=8, sentences=3, paragraphs=2), ['Ёж идёт домой.', 'Кот спит', 'Утро  наступило'])
[('Ёж идёт домой.', None), ('Кот спит', 'author'), ('Утро  наступило', None)]

docs.title: Parts of a document
docs.text:
Property Type Description text str The text tokens Tokens Tokens in order words Words Words in order multiword_tokens list[Token] Tokens of several words, in order sentences Sentences Sentences in order paragraphs Paragraphs Paragraphs in order lines Lines Lines of the paragraphs in order

The parts are views of the document, made when they are read; iterating over a collection makes them one at a time. Tokens, Words and the other collections are sequences (collections.abc.Sequence): they have a length, indices from the end and slices, and a slice with step 1 is a collection of the same kind. Two tokens, words, sentences, paragraphs or lines are equal when they are the same part of the same document; the collections compare by identity.

The collections of tokens, sentences, paragraphs and lines have starts and ends: the positions of their parts as lists of integers, made at once on every access. They are much faster than reading the parts one by one, and Document.from_tokens(doc.text, doc.tokens.starts, doc.tokens.ends) takes back the tokens of a document of the segmenter.

CodeResult 
token = doc.tokens[1]
token, token.spaces_after, token.sentence
doc.tokens[-2:], doc.sentences[2].paragraph
doc.sentences.starts, doc.sentences.ends

docs.title: Token
docs.text:
A token of the document: a span of its text.

Property Type Description index int Position of the token in the document, from 0 start, end int Position of the first character and the position after the last one text str Text of the token spaces_after str Text between the token and the next one, or the end of the text words Words Words of the token sentence Sentence Sentence of the token

docs.title: Word
docs.text:
A word of the document with its columns of CoNLL-U. Empty columns are None. The form of a word is the text of its token, except for the words of a multiword token, which the token holds together, and for a form read from CoNLL-U that differs from the text.

CodeResult 
spanish = Segmenter("es").segment("Vengo del mar")
[token.text for token in spanish.tokens], [word.form for word in spanish.words]

(['Vengo', 'del', 'mar'], ['Vengo', 'de', 'el', 'mar'])
Property Type Description index int Position of the word in the document, from 0 id int ID of the word in its sentence, from 1 form str Form of the word lemma, upos, xpos, feats, deprel, deps, misc str | None Columns of CoNLL-U head int | None ID of the head word in the sentence, 0 for the root token Token Token of the word sentence Sentence Sentence of the word

docs.title: Sentence
docs.text:
A sentence of the document: from the start of its first token to the end of its last one.

Property Type Description index int Position of the sentence in the document, from 0 start, end int Position of the first character and the position after the last one text str Text of the sentence tokens, words Tokens, Words Tokens and words of the sentence paragraph Paragraph Paragraph of the sentence

docs.title: Paragraph
docs.text:
A paragraph of the document: a part of its text between blank lines, from the start of its first token to the end of its last one.

Property Type Description index int Position of the paragraph in the document, from 0 start, end int Position of the first character and the position after the last one text str Text of the paragraph sentences, tokens Sentences, Tokens Sentences and tokens of the paragraph

docs.title: Line
docs.text:
A line of a paragraph, without the whitespace around it.

Property Type Description index int Position of the line in the document, from 0 start, end int Position of the first character and the position after the last one text str Text of the line break_before str | None How the line begins: None for the first line of a paragraph, "author" for a break the author made (a verse line, a list item, a paragraph per line), "typeset" for a wrap at the width of the page, as in text extracted from PDF

docs.title: Values of a column
docs.text:
column · list[str | None] / list[int | None]

column(name)

The values of a column of CoNLL-U, one per word: form, lemma, upos, xpos, feats, head, deprel, deps or misc. Empty values are None, heads are numbers. On a whole document the method is faster than reading the words one by one.

Parameter Type Default Description name str - Name of the column

Exceptions:

  • ValueError - there is no such column.

docs.title: Set columns
docs.text:
set_columns · None

set_columns(*, lemma=..., upos=..., xpos=..., feats=..., head=..., deprel=..., deps=..., misc=...)

Sets columns of the words, one value per word for every column given: all at once, or none if a value is wrong. None empties a value; a head is 0 or the ID of a word of its sentence. The forms come from the tokens and cannot be set.

Exceptions:

  • ValueError - there is no such column, a list has not one value per word, a value is empty, a lemma or MISC holds a tab or a line break or another value holds whitespace, or a head is out of its sentence;
  • TypeError - a value is neither a string nor None, or a head is not an integer.
CodeResult 
doc = Segmenter("ru").segment("Ёж идёт домой")
doc.set_columns(
    lemma=["ёж", "идти", "домой"],
    upos=["NOUN", "VERB", "ADV"],
    head=[2, 0, 2],
    deprel=["nsubj", "root", "advmod"],
)
doc.column("upos"), doc.column("head"), doc.words[0]

(['NOUN', 'VERB', 'ADV'], [2, 0, 2], Word(id=1, form='Ёж', lemma='ёж', upos='NOUN', head=2, deprel='nsubj'))

docs.title: Document in CoNLL-U
docs.text:
to_conllu · str

to_conllu(*, doc_id=None)

The document in CoNLL-U, every sentence followed by a blank line. A document read from CoNLL-U is written as it was read, with the columns set since. Otherwise every sentence gets the comments sent_id and text, the first one newdoc and every paragraph newpar, and the space after a token inside a paragraph goes to MISC: SpaceAfter=No when there is none and SpacesAfter when it is not one space. A multiword token has its line before the lines of its words, with the range of their IDs. Forms, the comment text and the values are in Unicode NFC, as CoNLL-U requires, and a lone surrogate is U+FFFD; the document keeps its text.

Parameter Type Default Description doc_id str None ID of the document: newdoc gets it and sent_id becomes ID-N, so that the sentences of several documents in one file have distinct IDs; a document read from CoNLL-U keeps its own comments and ignores it

Exceptions:

  • ValueError - the ID is empty or holds whitespace.
CodeResult 
print(doc.to_conllu(), end="")
print(Segmenter("ru").segment("Ёж идёт.  Кот спит").to_conllu(doc_id="news-1"), end="")

docs.title: Document of tokens
docs.text:
Document.from_tokens · Document

Document.from_tokens(text, starts, ends, *, sentence_starts=None, words=None)

The document of the tokens of a text made by another tool, one word per token except those given in words. Paragraphs are the parts of the text between blank lines, and every paragraph starts a sentence; without sentence starts a paragraph is one sentence.

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text starts Sequence[int] - Positions of the first characters of the tokens ends Sequence[int] - Positions after their last characters sentence_starts Sequence[int] None Indices of the tokens that start sentences words Mapping[int, Sequence[str]] None Forms of the words of the multiword tokens, by the index of the token

Exceptions:

  • ValueError - the lists differ in length, a token is empty, out of the text, overlaps the token before it, starts or ends with whitespace or runs over a paragraph boundary, the text between the tokens holds anything but whitespace and the invisible separators, the sentence starts are not increasing token indices, words names a token that is not in the document or has fewer than two forms, or a form is empty or holds a tab or a line break;
  • TypeError - a list holds something other than integers, or words is not a mapping of integers to sequences of strings.
CodeResult 
from anyseg import Document

doc = Document.from_tokens("Ёж идёт домой", [0, 3, 8], [2, 7, 13], sentence_starts=[0, 2])
[sentence.text for sentence in doc.sentences]

['Ёж идёт', 'домой']

docs.title: Reading CoNLL-U
docs.text:
read_conllu(text)

The documents of a text in CoNLL-U, in order. The comment newdoc starts a document and newpar a paragraph. The text of a sentence is its comment text or, without it, the forms of its tokens with the spaces of SpaceAfter and SpacesAfter; the sentences of a paragraph are joined by a space (none after SpaceAfter=No), the paragraphs by a blank line. Comments, the lines of multiword tokens and empty nodes are kept, so that to_conllu writes the text back as it was, with LF line ends. A byte order mark at the start is skipped.

Exceptions:

  • ValueError - the text does not end with a blank line, a line is neither a comment, a blank line nor a token line of 10 columns with plain numbers for IDs, in order, and for a head, a comment follows token lines, a sentence has no words or a multiword token misses some, or the forms do not match the text of their sentence or the text holds characters that no token has.
CodeResult 
from anyseg import read_conllu

conllu = "# text = Ёж идёт\n1\tЁж\tёж\tNOUN\t_\t_\t2\tnsubj\t_\t_\n2\tидёт\tидти\tVERB\t_\t_\t0\troot\t_\t_\n\n"
docs = read_conllu(conllu)
docs[0].words[1], docs[0].to_conllu() == conllu

(Word(id=2, form='идёт', lemma='идти', upos='VERB', head=0, deprel='root'), True)

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Python 3.11 or newer is required.

pip install anyseg

The package has no dependencies. The tokenizer and the sentence starts for spaCy come with the extra spacy:

pip install "anyseg[spacy]"

docs.title: Prebuilt wheels
docs.text:
PyPI hosts wheels for Linux (x86_64 and aarch64; manylinux and musllinux for Alpine), macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon) and Windows (x64 and arm64). One wheel serves every Python version starting with 3.11, and the free-threaded Python 3.14t and 3.15t have wheels of their own; Rust is not needed to install them. The free-threaded 3.13t is not supported.

Pre-release versions X.Y.Z.devN are published only on TestPyPI:

pip install --index-url https://test.pypi.org/simple/ --pre anyseg

docs.title: Building from source
docs.text:
On other platforms pip builds the package from source, which requires Rust 1.88 or newer:

curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh
pip install anyseg

The development environment is described in CONTRIBUTING.md.

docs.title: Rust
docs.text:
The segmenter is published on crates.io as the anyseg crate, with every language behind a Cargo feature, on by default: ru (Russian) and es (Spanish); cargo add anyseg --no-default-features --features es takes one. It gives positions in bytes of the UTF-8 string. The API documentation is on docs.rs.

cargo add anyseg

The command anyseg comes with the Python package; without Python, the crate installs it:

cargo install anyseg --features cli

docs.title: Russian
docs.text: Segmenter("ru") splits Russian text by the Universal Dependencies guidelines and, where they are silent, by the conventions of the largest Russian treebank, SynTagRus. Where the treebanks disagree, the rule follows what most of them do.

docs.title: Words
docs.text:
A word keeps its stress marks and soft hyphens, and a word with an apostrophe is one token.

CodeResult 
from anyseg import Segmenter

segmenter = Segmenter("ru")
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize("Ку́рица, До­ма, О'Нил, д’Артаньян")]

['Ку́рица', ',', 'До\xadма', ',', "О'Нил", ',', 'д’Артаньян']

docs.title: Abbreviations and initials
docs.text:
A common abbreviation keeps its period: «г.», «т.», «е.», «тыс.», «руб.», «им.», «окт.»; so does a single letter - an initial «А.» or a lowercase letter of an abbreviation, except the word «я». At the end of a sentence, the period of an abbreviation is a token of its own: «т. д.» at the end gives «т.», «д», «.». More abbreviations can be added to the segmenter.

CodeResult 
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize("В 1914 г. в Москве, т. е. в 2 тыс. км от А.С. Пушкина")]
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize("Купили груши и т. д.")]
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize("Это я.")]

['В', '1914', 'г.', 'в', 'Москве', ',', 'т.', 'е.', 'в', '2', 'тыс.', 'км', 'от', 'А.', 'С.', 'Пушкина']
['Купили', 'груши', 'и', 'т.', 'д', '.']
['Это', 'я', '.']

docs.title: Hyphenated words
docs.text:
A hyphenated word is one token: «кто-то», «кое-как», «мини-сауна», «вице-губернатор», «еле-еле», «Ту-154». It splits at the hyphen in these cases:

  • a particle after a hyphen - «-то», «-ка», «-таки», «-с», «-де»: «Вася-то», «скажи-ка»; indefinite pronouns and adverbs keep their «-то» («кто-то», «где-то»), and set phrases stay whole («всё-таки»);
  • a range or an approximate number: «1941-1945», «XIX-XX», «2,5-3,5», «два-три»;
  • a compound whose first part inflects, as the UD guidelines ask, where the segmenter can see it without a dictionary: two parts that end alike, as inflected forms do («учеными-энтузиастами», «человека-паука»), a word and a number («Формулы-1»), a name with «-на-» («Ростова-на-Дону»). Other compounds stay whole: «женщины-врача».
CodeResult 
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize("кто-то, кое-как, мини-сауна, еле-еле, Ту-154")]
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize("Вася-то, скажи-ка, всё-таки")]
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize("1941-1945, XIX-XX, два-три, 2,5-3,5")]
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize("Ростова-на-Дону, учеными-энтузиастами, Формулы-1")]

['кто-то', ',', 'кое-как', ',', 'мини-сауна', ',', 'еле-еле', ',', 'Ту-154']
['Вася', '-', 'то', ',', 'скажи', '-', 'ка', ',', 'всё-таки']
['1941', '-', '1945', ',', 'XIX', '-', 'XX', ',', 'два', '-', 'три', ',', '2,5', '-', '3,5']
['Ростова', '-', 'на', '-', 'Дону', ',', 'учеными', '-', 'энтузиастами', ',', 'Формулы', '-', '1']

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
Decimal numbers, numbers with groups of digits separated by spaces, dates with dots, times, three or more groups of digits joined by hyphens, as in phone numbers, and a number with a percent sign and an ending - «20%-ный» - are one token each. A phone number written with spaces or brackets and a date with slashes split.

CodeResult 
text = "4,5 и 1.5, 3 000 руб., 12.10.2026, 12:30, +7-495-123-45-67, 8 800 555 35 35, 15%, 20%-ный"
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize(text)]

['4,5', 'и', '1.5', ',', '3 000', 'руб.', ',', '12.10.2026', ',', '12:30', ',', '+7-495-123-45-67', ',', '8', '800', '555', '35', '35', ',', '15', '%', ',', '20%-ный']

docs.title: The web
docs.text:
URLs, e-mail addresses, domains and file names, mentions and hashtags are one token each, and so is a name of a service with a period: «Яндекс.Маркете». The punctuation that ends a sentence and a closing bracket that a URL did not open stay out of it.

CodeResult 
text = "Пишите на info@example.ru, сайт https://example.ru/news?id=5, файл config.yaml, @anna и #шопинг на Яндекс.Маркете"
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize(text)]

['Пишите', 'на', 'info@example.ru', ',', 'сайт', 'https://example.ru/news?id=5', ',', 'файл', 'config.yaml', ',', '@anna', 'и', '#шопинг', 'на', 'Яндекс.Маркете']

docs.title: Marks and symbols
docs.text:
A run of final marks is one token: «?!», «...», «!!!». So are an emoticon, a run of emoji with their modifiers, «°C» and a quote written as an HTML entity.

CodeResult 
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize("Ура!!! Что?! Ну... 20°C :) ))) 👍🏻 ❤️ "кот"")]

['Ура', '!!!', 'Что', '?!', 'Ну', '...', '20', '°C', ':)', ')))', '👍🏻', '❤️', '"', 'кот', '"']

docs.title: Sentences
docs.text:
A paragraph always starts a sentence. Inside it, a sentence ends at final marks - «.», «!», «?», «…» and their runs, with the closing quotes and brackets right after them - when a capital letter, a digit, an opening quote or bracket before a capital letter, or a dash before a capital letter follows - but not a source in brackets after a quotation: «…!» (Пушкин). A lowercase letter goes on with the sentence: the words of the author after a line of dialogue («— спросил он») and a thought after an ellipsis. A period without a space before a capital letter ends a sentence too.

CodeResult 
text = "Кот спит. Пёс лает! «Куда?» — спросил он. — Домой! — Он ушёл."
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize(text)]
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize("Ну и ну… и что? Тишина… Потом шум.")]
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize("Он пришел.Она ушла. В 10.30.Начали.")]

['Кот спит.', 'Пёс лает!', '«Куда?» — спросил он.', '— Домой!', '— Он ушёл.']
['Ну и ну… и что?', 'Тишина…', 'Потом шум.']
['Он пришел.', 'Она ушла.', 'В 10.30.', 'Начали.']

docs.title: Abbreviations
docs.text:
An abbreviation ends a sentence before a capital letter when the language lists it as one that usually stands at the end - «т. д.», «т. п.», «др.», «и пр.», «проч.», «н. э.», «тел.» - or when it follows a number: «в 1914 г.», «15 000 р.», «60 км/ч.». Other abbreviations and initials do not end a sentence: «г. Москва», «А. С. Пушкин». A single letter that is not an initial does: a Latin letter before a Russian word, as a variable or a name - «через x. Тогда», «Петра I. У него» - and a capital letter after a quantity, as a unit: «5 А. Напряжение», but not after a year, a date or a time: «в 12:00 В. Путин».

CodeResult 
text = "Купили груши и т. д. Потом ушли. Это было в г. Москва. В 1914 г. Затем всё. Пушкин А. С. Лермонтов"
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize(text)]
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize("Цена 15 000 р. Пишите. Едем 60 км/ч. Всё.")]
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize("Обозначим через x. Тогда ток 5 А. Напряжение 220 В.")]

['Купили груши и т. д.', 'Потом ушли.', 'Это было в г. Москва.', 'В 1914 г.', 'Затем всё.', 'Пушкин А. С. Лермонтов']
['Цена 15 000 р.', 'Пишите.', 'Едем 60 км/ч.', 'Всё.']
['Обозначим через x.', 'Тогда ток 5 А.', 'Напряжение 220 В.']

docs.title: Posts and messages
docs.text:
An emoticon or an emoji after final marks stays in the sentence; without them, it ends a sentence before a capital letter, as a period would. So does a closing bracket that no bracket opened, right after a word: «Спасибо) Завтра». A mention after final marks or an emoticon starts a sentence, and so does emphasis in Markdown before a capital letter: «Итог», «Курсив», «Жирный». A separator of stars - «* * », «**» - is a sentence of its own on a line of its own, or after final marks before a capital letter.

CodeResult 
text = "Привет 😀 Как дела? Ура! :) Пойдём. Спасибо! @anna да."
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize(text)]
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize("Текст. * * * Новая глава.")]
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize("Спасибо) Завтра увидимся. **Итог:** Всё хорошо.")]

['Привет 😀', 'Как дела?', 'Ура! :)', 'Пойдём.', 'Спасибо!', '@anna да.']
['Текст.', '* * *', 'Новая глава.']
['Спасибо)', 'Завтра увидимся.', '**Итог:** Всё хорошо.']

docs.title: Numbered items
docs.text:
A number with a period at the start of a paragraph or a line marks a list item and stays in its sentence, as the UD guidelines ask. So does a number of up to three digits inside a line before a capital letter: at the start of a sentence, when the sentence before or after it has the number next to it, and after a colon, when the sentence after it starts with the next number. Any other number with a period after the end of a sentence, before a capital letter, is a sentence of its own: a heading, a year, an answer.

CodeResult 
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize("План. 1. Прийти. 2. Уйти.")]
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize("1. Введение. Текст. 2. Обзор")]

['План.', '1. Прийти.', '2. Уйти.']
['1. Введение.', 'Текст.', '2.', 'Обзор']

docs.title: Paragraphs and lines
docs.text:
A paragraph is the part of the text between blank lines (or the paragraph separator U+2029). Inside a paragraph, a line break is a space, except where it starts a sentence:

  • before a list item - a bullet, an emoji, «1)», «1.», «а)» - or a line of dialogue;
  • at a line without words: «***», «-»;
  • after a line without final punctuation before a line with a capital letter: a heading, a line of a post. This rule is silent in text wrapped at the width of the page, where some line goes on with a lowercase letter, and in verse, except after a line without lowercase letters in a paragraph that has them, which is a heading. A paragraph reads as verse when some line ends with a comma or a semicolon before a line with a capital letter, or when its lines rhyme. Verse without rhymes and such marks splits by lines, as a post does.
CodeResult 
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize("Глава 1
Введение
Это текст главы. Он короткий.")]
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize("Нужно взять:
- паспорт
- СНИЛС
1) полис
✅ фото")]
verse = "Скажи-ка, дядя, ведь не даром
Москва, спалённая пожаром,
Французу отдана?
Ведь были ж схватки боевые"
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize(verse)]
rhymes = "Над тихой речкой встал туман
И скрыл прибрежные кусты
Отец уехал в дальний стан
И сжёг за собою мосты."
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize(rhymes)]

['Глава 1', 'Введение', 'Это текст главы.', 'Он короткий.']
['Нужно взять:', '- паспорт', '- СНИЛС', '1) полис', '✅ фото']
['Скажи-ка, дядя, ведь не даром
Москва, спалённая пожаром,
Французу отдана?', 'Ведь были ж схватки боевые']
['Над тихой речкой встал туман
И скрыл прибрежные кусты
Отец уехал в дальний стан
И сжёг за собою мосты.']

Every line of a document tells how it begins: "author" for a break the author made - a verse line, a list item, a paragraph per line - and "typeset" for a wrap at the width of the page, as in text extracted from PDF: outside verse, in a paragraph where some line goes on with a lowercase letter, a line that does not start a sentence.

CodeResult 
pdf = "Компания увеличила при-
быль на 15 %. Это
рекорд."
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize(pdf)]
[line.break_before for line in segmenter.segment(pdf).lines]

['Компания увеличила при-
быль на 15 %.', 'Это
рекорд.']
[None, 'typeset', 'typeset']

docs.title: Segmenter
docs.text:
Segmenter(lang, *, abbreviations=None, tokens=None)

Segmenter of texts in one language: it gives the tokens and the sentences of a text as spans of it, and the document of a text. The text is never changed, and a lone surrogate, as in JSON cut in the middle of a character, counts as U+FFFD and stays in the spans. A segmenter is immutable: create it once and use it throughout the program, from several threads at once, which segment long texts in parallel; it can be pickled and equals the segmenters of the same language and lists.

Exceptions:

  • ValueError - the language is not supported, an abbreviation is not a word of letters, or a token is empty, has whitespace or control characters or starts or ends with an invisible separator;
  • TypeError - abbreviations or tokens is a string or holds something other than strings.
CodeResult 
from anyseg import Segmenter

segmenter = Segmenter("ru")
segmenter.tokenize("Ёж идёт домой")

[Span(start=0, end=2, text='Ёж'), Span(start=3, end=7, text='идёт'), Span(start=8, end=13, text='домой')]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description lang str - ISO 639-1 code of the language: "ru", "es" abbreviations Iterable[str] None More abbreviations: words that keep a period after them tokens Iterable[str] None Strings that are one token each

The object keeps them read-only: lang is the code of the language, abbreviations and tokens are sorted tuples of the lists.

docs.title: Lists of your own
docs.text:
The rules of a language know the common abbreviations and the usual kinds of tokens; a text of a special field may need more.

  • Abbreviations are words that keep a period after them: "сущ" or "сущ.", in any case. Such a word with its period is one token and ends a sentence as the abbreviations of the language do: Russian, Spanish. The segmenter keeps them lowercase, without the period and the marks that the language leaves out of its lists.
  • Tokens are strings that are one token each, as written: "C++", "т.н.". A string matches where a token would start and no letter or digit adjoins it; of several strings that match at one place, the longest wins. Such a token is one word.
CodeResult 
custom = Segmenter("ru", abbreviations=["сущ."], tokens=["C++", "т.н."])
[span.text for span in custom.tokenize("Язык C++ - т.н. сущ. язык")]
custom

['Язык', 'C++', '-', 'т.н.', 'сущ.', 'язык']
Segmenter('ru', abbreviations=('сущ',), tokens=('C++', 'т.н.'))

docs.title: Tokens of a text
docs.text:
tokenize · list[Span]

tokenize(text)

The tokens of the text in order. Whitespace, control characters and the invisible separators - zero width space, word joiner, byte order mark, and a soft hyphen and zero width (non-)joiner outside a word - separate the tokens and are in none of them. How a language splits its text, see Russian and Spanish.

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text CodeResult 
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize("Ёж идёт, т. е. бежит: https://example.ru 😀")]

['Ёж', 'идёт', ',', 'т.', 'е.', 'бежит', ':', 'https://example.ru', '😀']

docs.title: Sentences of a text
docs.text:
sentenize · list[Span]

sentenize(text)

The sentences of the text in order, each from the start of its first token to the end of its last one. A paragraph - the part of the text between blank lines - always starts a sentence; inside it, final marks, abbreviations, emoticons and line breaks end sentences by the rules of the language: Russian, Spanish.

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text CodeResult 
text = "Кот спал в 1914 г. Затем ушёл. «Куда?» — спросил пёс."
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize(text)]
segmenter.sentenize(" Ёж идёт. Кот спит ")

['Кот спал в 1914 г.', 'Затем ушёл.', '«Куда?» — спросил пёс.']
[Span(start=1, end=9, text='Ёж идёт.'), Span(start=10, end=18, text='Кот спит')]

docs.title: Document of a text
docs.text:
segment · Document

segment(text)

The document of the text: its tokens as tokenize gives them, their words, its sentences as sentenize gives them, its paragraphs and their lines. A token holds several words where the language writes them together: Spanish «del» is «de» and «el». The document keeps the text and gives the parts as views of it.

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text CodeResult 
doc = segmenter.segment("Ёж идёт домой.\n\nКот спит")
[sentence.text for sentence in doc.sentences], len(doc.tokens)
[word.form for word in Segmenter("es").segment("Vengo del mar").words]

(['Ёж идёт домой.', 'Кот спит'], 6)
['Vengo', 'de', 'el', 'mar']

docs.title: Documents of texts
docs.text:
pipe · Iterator[Document]

pipe(texts, *, threads=1, batch_size=1000)

The documents of many texts, as segment gives them, in the order of the texts. The texts are taken from the iterable as the documents are asked for, batch_size at a time, and every batch is segmented without the GIL, on up to threads threads - at most one per core and per 4 KB of the batch: other Python threads run meanwhile, and several threads speed up a large collection of texts even with the GIL. A text that is not a string raises its error after the documents of the texts before it and ends the iteration, as does an error of the iterable; an interrupt such as KeyboardInterrupt comes at once. One iterator serves one thread at a time: a call while another runs raises ValueError.

Parameter Type Default Description texts Iterable[str] - Texts threads int 1 Number of threads that segment a batch batch_size int 1000 Number of texts in a batch

Exceptions:

  • ValueError - threads or batch_size is less than 1;
  • TypeError - texts is a string or not iterable, or a text is not a string.
CodeResult 
texts = ["Ёж идёт домой. Кот спит", "Утро", "Ночь  наступила"]
[len(doc.sentences) for doc in segmenter.pipe(texts, threads=2)]

[2, 1, 1]

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
tokenize(text, *, lang), sentenize(text, *, lang) and segment(text, *, lang) do the same as the methods of Segmenter(lang): the module keeps one segmenter per language. The language is a keyword argument and has no default.

CodeResult 
from anyseg import sentenize, tokenize

[span.text for span in tokenize("Мама мыла раму", lang="ru")]
[span.text for span in sentenize("Мама мыла раму. Кот спит", lang="ru")]

['Мама', 'мыла', 'раму']
['Мама мыла раму.', 'Кот спит']

docs.title: Span
docs.text:
Span(start, end, text)

A piece of a text with its position: start is the position of its first character, end the position after the last one, and text the piece. Positions are offsets in the characters of the Python string, as in its slices: text[span.start:span.end] == span.text. Spans are immutable, compare by all three attributes and can be pickled.

CodeResult 
from anyseg import Span

text = "Ёж идёт"
span = Span(3, 7, "идёт")
span, text[span.start : span.end] == span.text

(Span(start=3, end=7, text='идёт'), True)

docs.title: Rust
docs.text:
The segmenter is the Rust crate anyseg, with every language behind a Cargo feature, on by default: ru (Russian) and es (Spanish). It has the same Segmenter with tokenize, sentenize and segment, and gives positions in bytes of the UTF-8 string. segment_string takes a String without copying it, and ConlluWriter writes documents - the pieces of a long text - into one CoNLL-U, with the sentences numbered through them.

use anyseg::Segmenter;

let segmenter = Segmenter::new("ru").unwrap();
let text = "Мама мыла раму";
let tokens: Vec<&str> = segmenter.tokenize(text).iter().map(|span| span.slice(text)).collect();
assert_eq!(tokens, ["Мама", "мыла", "раму"]);

docs.title: spaCy
docs.text:
The tokenizer and the sentence starts of anySeg in a spaCy pipeline, and the conversion between a spaCy Doc and a document.

pip install "anyseg[spacy]"

The tokenizer and the component register with spaCy when the package is installed and are used by name, without importing anyseg. spaCy has no prebuilt wheels for the free-threaded Python 3.14t and 3.15t.

CodeResult 
import spacy

tokenizer = {"@tokenizers": "anyseg.Tokenizer.v1"}
nlp = spacy.blank("ru", config={"nlp": {"tokenizer": tokenizer}})
nlp.add_pipe("anyseg_sentencizer")
doc = nlp("В 1914 г. цена была 3 000 руб. Затем выросла")
[token.text for token in doc]
[sentence.text for sentence in doc.sents]

Sentencizer('ru')
['В', '1914', 'г.', 'цена', 'была', '3 000', 'руб', '.', 'Затем', 'выросла']
['В 1914 г. цена была 3 000 руб.', 'Затем выросла']

docs.title: Tokenizer
docs.text:
anyseg.Tokenizer.v1 is the tokenizer of the section [nlp.tokenizer] of a configuration. The text of a Doc is the text given, except that a lone surrogate, which spaCy cannot keep, is U+FFFD. One space after a token is its whitespace_, and the rest of the text between tokens - line breaks, more spaces, invisible separators - is a token of its own with is_space. nlp.tokenizer.pipe(texts, batch_size=1000) gives the documents of many texts, segmented in batches without the GIL as Segmenter.pipe does.

Parameter Type Default Description lang str None ISO 639-1 code of the language; by default the language of the pipeline abbreviations list[str] None More abbreviations tokens list[str] None Strings that are one token each CodeResult 
custom = {"@tokenizers": "anyseg.Tokenizer.v1", "tokens": ["C++"]}
nlp = spacy.blank("ru", config={"nlp": {"tokenizer": custom}})
[(token.text, token.whitespace_) for token in nlp("Язык C++\n\nКот  спит")]

[('Язык', ' '), ('C++', ''), ('\n\n', ''), ('Кот', ' '), (' ', ''), ('спит', '')]

The settings are in the configuration, so a saved pipeline loads with the tokenizer, and a pickled Doc of such a pipeline needs anySeg to load. A trained pipeline takes it when it is loaded:

nlp = spacy.load("ru_core_news_sm", config={"nlp": {"tokenizer": tokenizer}})

docs.title: Multiword tokens
docs.text:
The tokens of a Doc are those of the text, and the words of a multiword token are in its extension token._.anyseg_words: a list of dictionaries with their forms, and None for a token of one word or one that retokenizing changed.

CodeResult 
spanish = spacy.blank("es", config={"nlp": {"tokenizer": tokenizer}})
doc = spanish("Vengo del mar")
[token.text for token in doc], doc[1]._.anyseg_words

(['Vengo', 'del', 'mar'], [{'form': 'de'}, {'form': 'el'}])

The extension lives in the user data of a Doc:

  • a DocBin keeps it with store_user_data=True, as a tuple in place of the list, and Span.as_doc with copy_user_data=True;
  • Doc.from_docs keeps it by the positions in the text, so a Doc cut from a longer one should not hold keys of the part cut away;
  • Doc.to_json(underscore=["anyseg_words"]) needs a multiword token in the Doc, and Doc.from_json fails on a key of a token that was retokenized or cut away.

docs.title: Sentences
docs.text:
The component anyseg_sentencizer sets the sentence starts (is_sent_start) of a document as anySeg splits its text; before the parser it fixes the sentences, and the parser keeps them. It works with any tokenizer: a sentence starts at the token where its first character is, and the whitespace after a sentence stays in it.

nlp = spacy.load("ru_core_news_sm", config={"nlp": {"tokenizer": tokenizer}})
nlp.add_pipe("anyseg_sentencizer", before="parser")
Parameter Type Default Description lang str None ISO 639-1 code of the language; by default the language of the pipeline abbreviations list[str] None More abbreviations tokens list[str] None Strings that are one token each overwrite bool False Replace the sentence starts set before; False - set only the tokens whose start is unknown, as the sentencizer of spaCy does scorer Callable spacy.senter_scorer.v1 Scores of the sentences in an evaluation: sents_p, sents_r and sents_f, as for the sentencizer of spaCy CodeResult 
nlp = spacy.blank("ru")
nlp.add_pipe("anyseg_sentencizer")
[sentence.text for sentence in nlp("Кот спит в 1914 г. Затем\n\nУтро").sents]

Sentencizer('ru')
['Кот спит в 1914 г.', 'Затем\n\n', 'Утро']

With the tokenizer and the component, ru_core_news_sm 3.8.0 finds sentences and parses better. F1 of sentences and LAS on the test parts of the Russian treebanks of UD 2.18, from their raw text, every paragraph a document, scored with the evaluation script of CoNLL 2018. Comparison segments every test file as one text, so its F1 of sentences of the same pipeline is lower on Taiga, whose paragraphs often end without a final mark:

Test set Sentences, spaCy Sentences, anySeg LAS, spaCy LAS, anySeg SynTagRus 95.39 98.92 81.83 82.95 Taiga 80.42 89.92 71.55 73.39 GSD 85.85 96.32 75.80 79.34 PUD 96.45 99.25 86.14 87.26

With both, es_core_news_sm 3.8.0 does so on the test parts of the Spanish treebanks too. The parser reads the tokens of the text, and from_doc gives the words of the multiword tokens for the score:

Test set Sentences, spaCy Sentences, anySeg LAS, spaCy LAS, anySeg AnCora 97.70 98.66 80.43 82.06 GSD 88.14 90.97 69.35 71.09 PUD 97.34 98.80 73.35 74.57

The tokenizer gives 2.3 M tokens per second, nearly ten times as many as the tokenizer of spaCy; with the component, 1.4 M against 0.24 M with the sentencizer of spaCy (SynTagRus test, one thread, Apple M3 Pro). On AnCora test it gives 2.3 M against 0.42 M, and 1.6 M against 0.39 M.

docs.title: spaCy document of a document
docs.text:
anyseg.spacy.to_doc · Doc

to_doc(document, vocab)

The Doc of a document: its text, its tokens with the whitespace between them as the tokenizer makes it, and its sentences.

  • The columns lemma, upos, xpos and feats become lemma_, pos_, tag_ and morph where set. A whitespace token has its text for a lemma and SPACE for a part of speech.
  • Heads and relations are set when every word has a head, and the heads of every sentence must form a tree with one root. The relation root becomes ROOT, a word without a relation gets dep (a root - ROOT), and a whitespace token depends on the token before it with dep.
  • The words of a multiword token go to token._.anyseg_words with their columns: head is the ID of a word in its sentence, sentence_words the number of words in it, and main marks the word that gave the token its values, its word closest to the root or its first word without heads.
  • The vocabulary takes the rule of anySeg for is_space, so that a pickled document keeps it; a tokenizer of spaCy on that vocabulary then marks invisible separators as whitespace too.
Parameter Type Default Description document Document - Document vocab Vocab - Vocabulary of the pipeline

Exceptions:

  • ValueError - a token takes a part of speech that spaCy does not know, features that are not name=value pairs, or the heads of a sentence do not form a tree with one root.
CodeResult 
from anyseg import Segmenter
from anyseg.spacy import from_doc, to_doc

document = Segmenter("ru").segment("Ёж идёт.  Кот спит")
document.set_columns(upos=["NOUN", "VERB", "PUNCT", "NOUN", "VERB"])
doc = to_doc(document, nlp.vocab)
[(token.text, token.pos_) for token in doc]

[('Ёж', 'NOUN'), ('идёт', 'VERB'), ('.', 'PUNCT'), (' ', 'SPACE'), ('Кот', 'NOUN'), ('спит', 'VERB')]

docs.title: Document of a spaCy document
docs.text:
anyseg.spacy.from_doc · Document

from_doc(doc)

The document of a Doc, one word per token except those with token._.anyseg_words.

  • Tokens lose the whitespace and the invisible separators at their edges, and tokens of nothing else are dropped. A sentence of the Doc starts at its first token left, a Doc without sentences is a sentence per paragraph, and every paragraph starts a sentence.
  • lemma_, pos_, tag_, morph, the heads and dep_ become the columns lemma, upos, xpos, feats, head and deprel, empty values None, the features in the order of UD; a token without a head has neither. In a lemma, a line break or a tab becomes a space inside, with the spaces around it, and goes away at an edge.
  • The relation ROOT becomes root, and a word whose head is a dropped token depends on the head of that token. A sentence has one root: the root of the parse or, if the sentence lacks it, the first word whose head is in another sentence; the other such words depend on the root with dep.
  • The words of a multiword token keep the columns they have in the extension, but the word marked main takes the value of the token, even over an edit of that word in the extension. Without a mark, the first word takes the value for a column none of them has.
  • The heads of these words stay if every word has head and sentence_words, sentence_words is the number of words of the sentence, the head of the token is the head of one of its words, which then stands for the token, the marked one if it can, and the words form a tree; otherwise the first word takes the head and the relation of the token, and the other words depend on it with dep. A word of another token that depends on a word of a multiword token other than the one that stands for it moves to that one.
Parameter Type Default Description doc Doc - spaCy document

Exceptions:

  • ValueError - a token runs over a blank line, the extension is not a list of words with their forms or holds a form that cannot be in a document, or a value cannot be in its column, as for set_columns;
  • TypeError - a value of the extension is of a wrong type, as for set_columns.
CodeResult 
document = from_doc(doc)
document, document.words[3]

(Document(tokens=5, words=5, sentences=2, paragraphs=1), Word(id=1, form='Кот', upos='NOUN'))

docs.title: Spanish
docs.text: Segmenter("es") splits Spanish text by the Universal Dependencies guidelines and, where they are silent, by the conventions of the largest Spanish treebank, AnCora. Where the treebanks disagree, the rule follows AnCora.

docs.title: Words
docs.text:
A word keeps its accents and soft hyphens, and a word with an apostrophe or a similar mark inside is one token.

CodeResult 
from anyseg import Segmenter

segmenter = Segmenter("es")
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize("Cañón, pa­labra, O'Neal, O`Neal, d’Ebre, d´Ebre")]

['Cañón', ',', 'pa\xadlabra', ',', "O'Neal", ',', 'O`Neal', ',', 'd’Ebre', ',', 'd´Ebre']

docs.title: Abbreviations and initials
docs.text:
A common abbreviation keeps its period: «Sr.», «Dra.», «pág.», «p. ej.», «aprox.»; so does a single letter - an initial «J.» or a lowercase letter of an abbreviation, except the words «y», «e», «o», «u». Written without spaces, an abbreviation is one token: «EE.UU.», «S.A.». At the end of a sentence, its period is a token of its own.

Some forms keep the period only in context:

  • a form that is also a common word or a name, before a digit: «No. 45», «arts. 5 y 6», «Mar. 7», but «No. Se fue», «Electronic Arts. Luego»;
  • a word in capitals, before a digit or another word in capitals: «ART. 5», «EL SR. GARCÍA», but «Es del PP. Luego». «EE. UU.», «Ma.», «Cd.», «Vid.» and the commonest titles keep it anywhere: «DR. Juan Pérez».
CodeResult 
text = "El Sr. Pérez, p. ej., pág. 7, aprox. 5, la Dra. J. Ruiz en EE.UU. y S.A. hoy"
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize(text)]
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize("Compró peras, etc.")]
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize("La Ley No. 45. No. Se fue.")]
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize("ART. 5 y DR. Juan Pérez. Es del PP. Luego")]

['El', 'Sr.', 'Pérez', ',', 'p.', 'ej.', ',', 'pág.', '7', ',', 'aprox.', '5', ',', 'la', 'Dra.', 'J.', 'Ruiz', 'en', 'EE.UU.', 'y', 'S.A.', 'hoy']
['Compró', 'peras', ',', 'etc', '.']
['La', 'Ley', 'No.', '45', '.', 'No', '.', 'Se', 'fue', '.']
['ART.', '5', 'y', 'DR.', 'Juan', 'Pérez', '.', 'Es', 'del', 'PP', '.', 'Luego']

docs.title: Multiword tokens
docs.text:
A token can hold several words, as the UD guidelines ask for the words that Spanish writes together. The tokens stay those of the text, and a document gives their words:

  • the contractions «del» and «al» are «de» + «el» and «a» + «el»;
  • an infinitive or a gerund with pronouns is the verb, without the accent the pronouns brought, and the pronouns: «darlo», «dárselo», «viéndolo». Words that only look so stay whole: «parte», «muerte», «Reverte»;
  • frequent imperatives with pronouns and verbs with «os» are in tables: «dámelo», «cállate», «notifíquese», «deciros». Other such forms stay one word: «tranquilícese», «cantaros».

A form with a first capital letter is a name and stays whole after a word, a number or a comma, «El Al», and in quotes or brackets inside a sentence before another capital letter, «Vino (Del Bosque)». A string of the list of tokens stays one word.

CodeResult 
text = "Vengo del mar y voy al sol. Quiero dárselo, viéndolo bien. Dímelo, tranquilícese, es parte de El Al."
doc = segmenter.segment(text)
[(token.text, [word.form for word in token.words]) for token in doc.multiword_tokens]
print(segmenter.segment("Vengo del mar").to_conllu(), end="")

[('del', ['de', 'el']), ('al', ['a', 'el']), ('dárselo', ['dar', 'se', 'lo']), ('viéndolo', ['viendo', 'lo']), ('Dímelo', ['Di', 'me', 'lo'])]
# newdoc
# newpar
# sent_id = 1
# text = Vengo del mar
1   Vengo   _   _   _   _   _   _   _   _
2-3 del _   _   _   _   _   _   _   _
2   de  _   _   _   _   _   _   _   _
3   el  _   _   _   _   _   _   _   _
4   mar _   _   _   _   _   _   _   _

docs.title: Hyphens and marks inside a token
docs.text:
A hyphenated word and a range are one token: «franco-alemán», «1990-1995», «XIX-XX», «2,5-3,5»; so is a range with an en dash, between digits or between Roman numbers: «1990–1995», «XIX–XX». A slash and a plus stay inside a token between letters or digits: «km/h», «I+D», «15/01/2011». With a space beside them, these marks are tokens of their own. A superscript digit is always a token of its own: «km²».

CodeResult 
text = "franco-alemán, sub-23, 1990-1995, 1990–1995, XIX-XX, 2,5-3,5"
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize(text)]
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize("km/h, y/o, I+D, 15/01/2011, 30/1.992, a / b")]
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize("10 km², 5 m/s²")]

['franco-alemán', ',', 'sub-23', ',', '1990-1995', ',', '1990–1995', ',', 'XIX-XX', ',', '2,5-3,5']
['km/h', ',', 'y/o', ',', 'I+D', ',', '15/01/2011', ',', '30/1.992', ',', 'a', '/', 'b']
['10', 'km', '²', ',', '5', 'm/s', '²']

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
One token each are decimal numbers with a comma, groups of three digits with points or, as in Mexico and Central America, with commas and a decimal point, times, three or more groups of digits joined by hyphens, as in phone numbers, and ordinal numbers with their ending or a degree sign. A minus before a digit is in the number after a space or an opening mark. Digits separated by spaces and a percent sign are tokens of their own.

CodeResult 
text = (
    "20.000, 1.500,50, 0,4, 1,500.50, 12:30, 3.º, 2.ª, 1.er, 1°, N.° 5, de -5 grados, 3 000, 15%"
)
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize(text)]

['20.000', ',', '1.500,50', ',', '0,4', ',', '1,500.50', ',', '12:30', ',', '3.º', ',', '2.ª', ',', '1.er', ',', '1°', ',', 'N.°', '5', ',', 'de', '-5', 'grados', ',', '3', '000', ',', '15', '%']

docs.title: The web
docs.text:
URLs, e-mail addresses, domains, «lanacion.com.ar» among them, file names, mentions and hashtags are one token each, without the punctuation that ends a sentence. A top-level domain that is a Spanish word starts a sentence after a missing space when it has a first capital letter: «casa.De pronto», but «Amazon.Com».

CodeResult 
text = "Escribe a info@ejemplo.es, en https://ejemplo.es/noticias?id=5, el archivo datos.csv, @ana y #fútbol."
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize(text)]
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize("En casa.De, Amazon.Com, lanacion.com.ar")]

['Escribe', 'a', 'info@ejemplo.es', ',', 'en', 'https://ejemplo.es/noticias?id=5', ',', 'el', 'archivo', 'datos.csv', ',', '@ana', 'y', '#fútbol', '.']
['En', 'casa', '.', 'De', ',', 'Amazon.Com', ',', 'lanacion.com.ar']

docs.title: Marks and symbols
docs.text:
A run of one final mark is one token: «...», «!!»; different final marks are apart. «¿» and «¡» are tokens one by one. An emoticon, «:v» and «xD» among them, a run of emoji with their modifiers and «°C» are one token each.

CodeResult 
[span.text for span in segmenter.tokenize("¡¡Hola!! ¿Qué?! Bueno... 20°C :) 👍🏻 ❤️")]

['¡', '¡', 'Hola', '!!', '¿', 'Qué', '?', '!', 'Bueno', '...', '20', '°C', ':)', '👍🏻', '❤️']

docs.title: Sentences
docs.text:
A paragraph always starts a sentence. Inside it, a sentence ends at final marks - «.», «!», «?», «…» and their runs, with the closing quotes and brackets right after them - before a capital letter, a digit or an inverted mark, maybe after an opening quote, a bracket or a dash. «¿» and «¡» start a sentence before a lowercase letter too, unless an ellipsis comes before them or they are glued to the mark; any other lowercase letter goes on. A period without a space ends a sentence before a capital letter, not before a number: «casa.Es», «j.ejemplo.2020».

CodeResult 
text = '¿Qué hora es? ¡Claro! ¡qué bien! Se fue. ¿por qué? Se fue. "¿por qué?"'
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize(text)]
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize("Bueno... ¿qué dices? Tal vez… Luego.")]
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize("Vino a casa.Es tarde.")]

['¿Qué hora es?', '¡Claro!', '¡qué bien!', 'Se fue.', '¿por qué?', 'Se fue.', '"¿por qué?"']
['Bueno... ¿qué dices?', 'Tal vez…', 'Luego.']
['Vino a casa.', 'Es tarde.']

docs.title: Dialogue and articles
docs.text:
A dash starts a line of dialogue before a capital letter, a digit or an inverted mark; before a lowercase letter it brings the words of the author, which stay in the line.

A sentence goes on after these dashes:

  • a hyphen right after a period, with or without a space after it: «Artículo 1.- Objeto», «Artículo 1.-Objeto»;
  • a longer dash after a number, a word in capitals or a sentence of one word: «Artículo 1.— Objeto», «PRIMERO.—Se aprueba», «Primero.— Se aprueba»;
  • the longer dash of a dateline: «MADRID, 12 ene. (EFE).— El Gobierno».

After other text, a longer dash with a space after it closes its sentence: «La viuda.-- El niño».

CodeResult 
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize("—¿Vienes? —preguntó ella. —Sí. —Y se fue.")]
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize("¿Cuánto? —5 euros. La viuda.-- El niño lloró.")]
text = "Artículo 1.-Objeto de la ley. Artículo 2.— Ámbito."
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize(text)]

['—¿Vienes? —preguntó ella.', '—Sí.', '—Y se fue.']
['¿Cuánto?', '—5 euros.', 'La viuda.--', 'El niño lloró.']
['Artículo 1.-Objeto de la ley.', 'Artículo 2.— Ámbito.']

docs.title: Abbreviations
docs.text:
An abbreviation ends a sentence before a capital letter, but not before a round bracket, in these cases:

  • the language lists it as one that usually stands at the end: «etc.», «a. C.», «EE. UU.», «Ud.», «Ltda.», «et al.», «y ss.»;
  • it follows a number, as a unit does, in lowercase, «Mide 5 cm.», or in capitals with periods, «10:30 A.M.», unless it belongs to an address, a title or an edition: «Calle 15 esq. Centro», «3.ª ed. Madrid»;
  • a single capital letter or capitals with periods inside stand inside a sentence before a word that seldom follows an initial: «Felipe V. El rey», «Empresa S.A. En 2001». Such words as «El», «La» and «Su» cost a name now and then: «Vino M. El Baradei»;
  • a capital letter follows a quantity, as a unit: «Son 5 A. Pesa», but not a year, a date or a time: «Vino en 1990 A. Pérez», «A las 12.30 A. Pérez».

Other abbreviations and initials do not end a sentence: «el Sr. Pérez», «J. L. Borges», «A.M. Turing».

CodeResult 
text = "Compró peras, etc. Luego se fue. Murió en 44 a. C. Vive en EE. UU. Trabaja. Mide 5 cm. Pesa 3 kg."
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize(text)]
text = "Vino el Sr. Pérez. Calle 15 esq. Centro. Vino J. L. Borges."
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize(text)]
text = "Fue Felipe V. El rey vino. Fue Carlos I. La visita acabó."
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize(text)]
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize("A las 10:30 A.M. Salió. Empresa S.A. En 2001 cerró.")]

['Compró peras, etc.', 'Luego se fue.', 'Murió en 44 a. C.', 'Vive en EE. UU.', 'Trabaja.', 'Mide 5 cm.', 'Pesa 3 kg.']
['Vino el Sr. Pérez.', 'Calle 15 esq. Centro.', 'Vino J. L. Borges.']
['Fue Felipe V.', 'El rey vino.', 'Fue Carlos I.', 'La visita acabó.']
['A las 10:30 A.M.', 'Salió.', 'Empresa S.A.', 'En 2001 cerró.']

docs.title: Posts and messages
docs.text:
An emoticon or an emoji after final marks stays in the sentence; without them, it ends a sentence before a capital letter or an inverted mark. A mention after final marks or an emoticon starts a sentence, and so does emphasis in Markdown before a capital letter. A separator of stars is a sentence of its own on a line of its own, or after final marks before a capital letter.

CodeResult 
text = "Hola 😀 ¿Qué tal? ¡Bien! :) Vamos. Gracias! @ana sí."
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize(text)]
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize("Texto. * * * Nuevo capítulo.")]

['Hola 😀', '¿Qué tal?', '¡Bien! :)', 'Vamos.', 'Gracias!', '@ana sí.']
['Texto.', '* * *', 'Nuevo capítulo.']

docs.title: Numbered items
docs.text:
A number with a period at the start of a paragraph or a line marks a list item and stays in its sentence, as the UD guidelines ask. So does a number of up to three digits, or a small Roman number, inside a line before a capital letter: at the start of a sentence, when the sentence before or after it has the number next to it, and after a colon, when the sentence after it starts with the next number. Any other number with a period after the end of a sentence, before a capital letter, is a sentence of its own: a heading, a year, an answer.

CodeResult 
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize("Plan. 1. Llegar. 2. Salir.")]
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize("1. Introducción. Texto. 2. Método")]
[span.text for span in segmenter.sentenize("EXPONEN: I. Que tal. II. Que cual.")]

['Plan.', '1. Llegar.', '2. Salir.']
['1. Introducción.', 'Texto.', '2.', 'Método']
['EXPONEN: I. Que tal.', 'II. Que cual.']

docs.title: Paragraphs and lines
docs.text:
A paragraph is the part of the text between blank lines (or the paragraph separator U+2029). Inside a paragraph, a line break is a space, except where it starts a sentence:

  • before a list item - a bullet, a number with a minus, an emoji, «1)», «1.», «a)» - or a line of dialogue;
  • at a line without words: «***», «-»;
  • after a line without final punctuation before a line with a capital letter, maybe after the number of a section: a heading, a line of a post, «1.2 Métodos». This rule is silent in text wrapped at the width of the page, where some line goes on with a lowercase letter, and in verse, except after a line without lowercase letters in a paragraph that has them, which is a heading. A paragraph reads as verse when some line ends with a comma or a semicolon before a line with a capital letter, or when its lines rhyme. Verse without rhymes and such marks splits by lines, as a post does.
CodeResult 
text = "Capítulo 1
Introducción
